headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict: Haystack can ingest Argo outputs via APIs/MCP while broad egress can propagate unverified results.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can emit artifacts over REST/GRPC, and Haystack can consume external content via REST APIs and MCP servers. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled workflow output is treated as instructions or context. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Argo-produced artifacts are forwarded into Haystack prompts or tools without sanitization
IF an MCP server exposes workflow outputs as trusted context
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every Argo artifact before Haystack reads it
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported content
Restrict Haystack MCP tools to read-only endpoints
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while Haystack has broad network egress and can send data to external services. Even though the profiles do not show shared storage, the pair can still move workflow data into Haystack outputs or remote calls in default integrations. The evidence is indirect, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF artifacts or parameters from Argo are passed into Haystack retrieval or generation
IF Haystack forwards those inputs to a third-party API
mitigations: Remove sensitive fields from Argo artifacts before handoff
Set Haystack egress to a strict allowlist
Turn off logging of prompt/context payloads
requires-engineering: isolate the two systems with separate workspaces and credentials

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo has API-driven workflow control and Haystack can act through REST APIs and MCP servers, so both can mutate shared external resources if orchestrated together. The profiles do not prove a shared writable directory or lock manager, so I cannot justify high; uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same downstream API or datastore
IF no external locking or optimistic concurrency is enabled
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts per agent
Add a mutex or lease around shared writes
Limit one agent to read-only access on shared resources
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination for shared mutable targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce workflow artifacts and Haystack is an LLM/RAG system that may render or act on retrieved content. If Haystack treats Argo output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. Because the pair lacks verification controls in the profiles and the blast radius can span multiple work products, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Haystack uses Argo outputs as retrieval context without validation
IF downstream consumers act on Haystack-generated answers
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Haystack uses Argo output
Require citations or source IDs for every derived claim
Mark Argo outputs as untrusted until checked
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between workflow artifacts and RAG answers

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only show artifacts/parameters versus anonymous usage statistics, so there is no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch evidence. The main compliance concern is limited logging or retention drift if Argo data is forwarded into Haystack, but that is not documented here. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, though no specific mismatch is proven.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Argo into Haystack logs or telemetry
IF retention policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated fields into Haystack telemetry
Document retention settings for both systems
Purge test data from shared environments
requires-engineering: align data-handling policies before production use
